lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good morning Barbara! Thanks for picking up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, yes, perfect timing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the walking went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, that sounds good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How's your energy been this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've had more energy, I noticed that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's great to hear.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Tell me how the walking went this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Honestly, not much. With all the rain I just stayed in.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the walking fit in your day?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't really see the point.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm too tired for this right now.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It feels like a lot right now.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You need to walk every day, no excuses.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I think I can do 20 minutes if it's early.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You think you can do it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Just get out there, even when it's hot.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know, I know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you try the mall?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people walk inside the mall early, before the stores open. It's cool and it's flat.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, walking hurts my knees, so why bother.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe after the summer.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're not sure it's worth it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't feel safe walking around here. At least I'm trying.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd walk more if you had a place that felt safe.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Next week I want you to walk 30 minutes on 5 days.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, but you don't know my schedule.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Barbara, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

tags.note: Directive with no excuses; pushes change
Plan the night before, ability to do it
Pushes action despite heat; ignores change talk
Links walking to safe place; safety not explored
Imposes 30 min on 5 days without collaboration

flags.reason: Repeated directives ('You need to walk every day, no excuses', 'must make this a priority') with no permission; participant disengages.
Fear-based warning about health suffering shuts down discussion of knee pain and motivation.
Coach ignored confidence statements at 21, 23 and 37 and moved to prescribing a new goal.
Set 30 min on 5 days without asking her view; she pushed back ('you don't know my schedule') and it was not addressed.
Participant said she doesn't feel safe walking locally; coach reflected but did not explore safety or alternatives.

score.summary: The coach opened well and asked about energy and last week's walking, but then relied heavily on directives and warnings (lines 14, 18, 24, 32, 38) that overrode Barbara's stated barriers and confidence. Barbara's change talk (lines 21, 23, 37) and her unsafe-neighborhood concern (line 35) went unexplored, and the goal was imposed rather than co-created.
strengths: Line 5 and 8: opened with open questions about energy and walking, following the agenda.
Line 13: 'It's completely your call' briefly offered autonomy.
Line 22: simple reflection of her ability ('You think you can do it') acknowledged her confidence.
Line 40: clear follow-up plan with a midweek text.
coaching_tips: Line 38: Ask permission before proposing a goal, e.g., 'Would it help to talk about a walking goal that fits your schedule?'
Line 18 and 24: Replace 'no excuses' directives with reflections, e.g., 'Walking early feels doable for you, and the heat and rain make it harder.'
Line 32: Avoid warnings about health; explore her own reasons with 'What matters most to you about your energy right now?'
Line 35: Explore the unsafe-feeling walking area with an open question, e.g., 'Tell me more about what makes it feel unsafe.'
Line 37: Build on change talk with a follow-up like 'What helped you do it before?' and summarize her plan from line 23.
